items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: hardly anybody extracted for Duke except Tom Whale or myself

ctx.x: I have heard a couple of people say that Duke writes, or wrote, in in his own kind of 'shorthand' musically, and that you really had to know the way Duke did it, and that anybody who could normally read music would not understand how to extract for Duke. Is that right?

Well, in a way, that is right. But it's a case that hardly anybody extracted for Duke except Tom Whale or myself. But I did most of the extraction; for Duke, I did all of the extraction myself, because we did it with pencil, no ink or nothing.
I remember seeing you work with Duke, you know, later, in later years, but even after you were no longer with the band, you were still doing extracting for Duke.

items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: Juan Tizol, he did the copying before I come in there, see and Juan said no, I ain't going blind copying Duke's music.

ctx.x: Juan Tizol, he did the copying before I come in there, see and Juan said no, I ain't going blind copying Duke's music. Well, I never had that -- no, I never thought about going blind because the woman doctor had told me I had good eye and I used to go up to the medical center there at 153rd Street and the man used to give me drops for it. But it seemed like it went, I overstrained it.
But you sure copied a lot of -- tell us something about your relationship with Duke, since we're into this thing about your eyes, because you and him were pretty close.
